div.div: Fails → the container is killed and restarted. Wrong tool for a slow boot.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 758px; height: 1px; padding-top: 501px; margin-left: 38px;

div.div: No readiness probe → the rollout marks a pod ready the moment it starts, and sends real traffic to a process still building its first render.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 551px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: What a frontend owes this platform is small and concrete: an image that starts fast, a readiness endpoint that tells the truth, config read at runtime, and assets served from the CDN rather than from a pod.
